daily_reality.summary: EMTs respond to emergency 911 calls providing basic life support, patient assessment, and transport. They work 12-24 hour shifts in ambulances, fire departments, and hospitals. High-stress, physically demanding work with unpredictable schedules.
typical_tasks: Responding to 911 emergency calls via ambulance
Performing patient assessment: vitals, chief complaint, medical history
Administering basic life support: CPR, AED defibrillation, airway management
Controlling bleeding, splinting fractures, managing spinal immobilization
Starting IVs and administering approved medications (scope varies by state)
Transporting patients safely to emergency departments
Communicating patient status to receiving hospital via radio
Completing patient care reports (PCRs) and documentation
Maintaining and checking ambulance equipment at shift start
Participating in public education and community CPR training

deadlines.response_time: 6-8 minutes average target for emergency calls
deadlines.nremt_recertification: Every 2 years — 40 hours CE for EMT, 48 hours for AEMT
deadlines.state_license_renewal: Varies by state — typically every 2-4 years

daily_reality.seasonality: Summer brings increased trauma (vehicle accidents, outdoor injuries, heat-related illness). Winter brings hypothermia, slip-and-fall injuries. Holiday periods see increased alcohol-related calls.

regulatory.summary: National certification through NREMT. State licensing varies. Three EMT levels: EMT-Basic, AEMT (Advanced), Paramedic. Scope of practice defined by state medical director protocols. OSHA standards for bloodborne pathogens and PPE.

key_laws.name: NREMT certification requirements
key_laws.description: National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians sets national certification standards

key_laws.name: Good Samaritan laws (vary by state)
key_laws.description: Legal protection for emergency responders acting in good faith

requirements: Complete state-approved EMT course (120-150 hours for EMT-Basic)
Recertification every 2 years with 40 hours CE

regulatory.recent_changes: Growing advocacy for higher EMT wages at federal level. Some states expanding EMT scope of practice. Community paramedicine programs expanding. Ongoing debate about EMS workforce crisis and funding models.

tools.summary: Ambulance-based medical equipment, ePCR documentation systems, radio communications, and patient monitoring devices. Technology focused on field reliability and rapid deployment.

primary_tools.name: Automated External Defibrillator (AED/Monitor)
primary_tools.examples: ZOLL X Series, Philips HeartStart, Physio-Control LIFEPAK

primary_tools.name: ePCR (Electronic Patient Care Report) software
primary_tools.description: Tablet-based documentation for all patient encounters

primary_tools.name: Airway management equipment
primary_tools.description: BVM (bag-valve mask), supraglottic airways, suction devices, oxygen systems

primary_tools.name: Radio communication systems
primary_tools.description: Radio for dispatch, hospital notification, and crew coordination

primary_tools.name: Vital signs monitoring equipment
primary_tools.description: Pulse oximeters, blood pressure cuffs, glucometers, thermometers

primary_tools.name: Patient transport equipment
primary_tools.description: Power stretchers, stair chairs, backboards, scoop stretchers

secondary_tools: Triage tags and mass casualty incident kits
Personal protective equipment (gloves, gowns, N95 masks)
pain_points: Outdated equipment and ambulances in underfunded agencies
Bulky ePCR systems that slow down documentation
Radio dead zones and communication failures
Lack of ergonomic patient lifting equipment
Limited technology integration between agencies and hospitals

terminology.summary: EMS-specific vocabulary combining medical terminology, radio communication codes, and field operations language.

terms.NREMT: National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians
terms.PCR: Patient Care Report — documentation for each call
terms.AVPU: Alert, Verbal, Pain, Unresponsive — rapid consciousness assessment
terms.SAMPLE: Signs/Symptoms, Allergies, Medications, Past history, Last intake, Events — history mnemonic
terms.OPQRST: Onset, Provocation, Quality, Radiation, Severity, Time — pain assessment
terms.START triage: Simple Triage and Rapid Treatment — field triage system
terms.transport: Moving patient to hospital by ambulance
terms.IFT: Interfacility transfer — transport between medical facilities

career_psychology.summary: Mission-driven but severely underpaid profession. 76% burnout rate. 37% planning to leave within 5 years. 45% earn $19/hour or less. NYC projected to lose 1/3 of EMTs in 2026 due to pay disparity. High emotional and physical toll offset by deep sense of purpose.
career_path: Entry-level EMT at ambulance service, fire department, or hospital
Advanced EMT (AEMT) certification with additional training
EMS captain / battalion chief / operations manager
Transition to nursing, physician assistant, or other healthcare career
fears: PTSD from traumatic calls (pediatric deaths, mass casualties)
Personal safety on scene (violence, traffic, hazmat)
Physical injuries from lifting and patient handling
Liability from clinical decisions in high-pressure situations
motivation: Saving lives and making immediate difference
Adrenaline and excitement of emergency response
Community service and public safety mission
burnout_factors: 37% plan to leave EMS within 5 years
61% cite lack of time for physical health
Only 59% of agencies have enough staff to answer 911 calls
NYC: 1/3 of EMTs expected to quit in 2026 due to pay

community.summary: Community organized through NAEMT, NREMT, state EMS associations, and fire service unions. Strong online presence on EMS forums and social media. EMS Week (third week of May) is the major professional celebration.

market.summary: Growing demand (11% projected growth) but severe workforce crisis. 76% burnout rate and low wages driving mass exodus. Only 59% of agencies fully staffed. NYC projected to lose 1/3 of workforce in 2026. Industry needs ~439,000 additional workers.

market_trends: Severe EMS workforce crisis — 76% burnout rate driving departures
Growing community paramedicine programs (expanded EMT roles)
Advocacy for higher wages and benefits at federal/state level
Mental health support programs expanding in EMS agencies
Some agencies offering signing bonuses and tuition reimbursement
